info.description:
## Proxy-Cheap uses REST API to enable proxy ordering.

This is Proxy-Cheap documentation for developers interested in integrating our services in your product. We offer 2 types of APIs currently:

- **REST API**: Calls made by you to do a requested operation
    
- **Webhooks**: Calls made by us, you consume them
    

Pick a type from the sidebar to know more.

**Contact Support:**  
Email: [support@proxy-cheap.com](https://mailto:support@proxy-cheap.com)

request.description: This endpoint is the entry point to the whole ordering process. It returns the list of orderable services, and optionally their plans when supported. The service and plan identifiers are required to be included within payloads of all the remaining endpoints: setup, price & execute.

response.name: Successful operation

variable.description: The identifier of the chosen service returned by the Services endpoint.

request.description:
Endpoint `/v2/order/:serviceId` allows you to fetch all the order properties available for the selected service. Some of the services might require a `planId` - refer to the plans available under the specific service in the `/v2/order` endpoint. Each service might be described by different properties, so you shouldn't assume they all work the same way.

As an example - only the `static-residential-ipv4` returns the `isps` property, while the `rotating-residential` and `rotating-mobile` don't return any additional information because the only thing required for their purchase is the allocated traffic specified in GB.

item.description:
## Proxy-Cheap uses REST API to enable proxy ordering.

Authentication is implemented using API keys passed as HTTP headers with each request. Use `X-Api-Key` and `X-Api-Secret` obtained at our dashboard [https://app.proxy-cheap.com/api-keys](https://app.proxy-cheap.com/api-keys).

All request and response payloads are in JSON format.

---

**Usage**:

1. Fetch the available services & plans using the _Services_ endpoint.
    
2. Fetch the available configuration like countries, ISPs, packages, etc using the _Setup_ endpoint.
    
3. Price the selected configuration using the _Price_ endpoint.
    
4. Order the selected configuration using the _Execute_ endpoint.
    

**Contact Support:**  
Email: [support@proxy-cheap.com](https://mailto:support@proxy-cheap.com)

item.name: Webhooks

request.description:
Whenever we schedule maintenace window, or we detect that server is down, we dispatch this event.

Default time window when detecting that server is down is `24H`. If server is back online, we will fire `proxy.maintenance_window.cancelled` event.

Whenever the status of our proxies changes, we will fire this webhook. Currently recognized statuses are following:

- `PENDING`
    
- `INITIATING`
    
- `ACTIVE`
    
- `EXPIRED`
    
- `CANCELED`

item.description:
# 🪝 Introduction

Webhooks are a mechanism that allows services to send real-time notifications to your application regarding asynchronous updates. This collection contains example payloads and events that we are sending from Proxy-Cheap to your webhook endpoints.

Bear in mind though that you have to create webhook configuration on [our webhook configuration section](https://app.proxy-cheap.com/webhooks). Once you create webhook configuration, you _should_ get a **secret** from there so that you can validate on your side when webhook is legitimate and not spoofed.

## Webhook request structure

### Headers

- **Webhook-Event:** Name of the event. Important for distinguishing actions you are interested on your side. Currently supported events:
    
    - `proxy.maintenance_window.created`
        
    - `proxy.maintenance_window.cancelled`
        
    - `proxy.status.changed`
        
    - `proxy.bandwidth.added`
        
- **Webhook-Id:** ID of the event. Currently it's autogenerated and its payload has no bearing on it. However, in future we might consider using it to ensure indepotence
    
- **Content-Type:** Specifies format of the payload. Currently, we always use `application/json`
    
- **Webhook-Signature:** Signature of the payload. Explained in next section
    

### **Body**

Body of the payload depends on which event is being sent. Please see example requests in this collection, there should be an example for each event.

## 🔐 Webhook signature verification

We are using HMAC hash sent together with webhook request as `Webhook-Signature` header. Beginning of the value is hash algorithm used separated by `=`. Input for HMAC hash are following values concatenated:

- hash algorithm (currently we use `sha256`)
    
- event name (from header)
    
- event ID (from header)
    
- body
    
- secret (from when you add a new webhook configuration on our side)
    

Here is a an example value: `sha256=b32e17dd8fb808f11a706f002ee598bb5e26fcef867105303800d072c7fac9b5`

And here is a code used for generating it:

```
$this->algo.'='.hash_hmac($this->algo, $event->getName().$event->getId().$body, $secret)

 ```

If you would like to ensure your signature verification works, please try it with our example requests, secret used there is `0qFbBP1zE5MuSMy`. Bear in mind that unlike what these postman examples show, payload is in reality minified instead of prettyfied.

## Considerations

Please ensure that your webhook consuming endpoint is reacting reasonably fast. We will send each event once only, we don't retry them.

## ℹ️ Resources

[Symfony webhook component](https://symfony.com/doc/current/webhook.html): If you use Symfony, this is a component that's compatible with HTTP requests we are sending.
